title: Creating Two-Dimensional Patterned Substrates for Protein and Cell Confinement
protocol: Center the silicon wafer on the spin-coater.
Rinse the wafer with acetone during the initial step of the two-cycle spin program.
Apply approximately 1 mL AZ9245 photoresist to the wafer and spin-coat using conditions described in Table 1.
Soft-bake the photoresist-coated wafer at 110°C for 2 minutes using a high-uniformity hotplate.
Photopattern the substrate using either a direct-write photolithography system or a mask aligner system with appropriate mask.
Develop the patterned wafer in 1:2 400K developer:semi-conductor grade deionized water for 1 minute 45 seconds with gentle agitation.
Rinse thoroughly with semi-conductor grade deionized water.
Dry the wafer with a stream of nitrogen (N2) gas.
Prepare a 10:1 by weight resin:hardener mixture of Sylgard 182 (PDMS).
Completely cover the master (photopatterned wafer) with the PDMS mixture in a disposable petri dish.
De-gas the PDMS-covered master in a vacuum dessicator until no bubbles are visible.
Allow the stamp to cure in an oven at 65°C for 1.5 h.
Cut the PDMS stamp out of the master and trim to the appropriate size.
Store the stamp in a covered container (feature side up) to protect it from dust and debris.
Prepare 25 mm no. 1 round glass coverslips by treating them with oxygen plasma for 10 min.
Rinse the coverslips twice with 18.2 MΩ deionized water followed by ethanol rinsing twice.
Dry the coverslips with a stream of N2 gas between each step.
Deposit 50 Å titanium and 150 Å gold on the prepared glass coverslips using an electron-beam deposition system without venting the evaporator between layers.
Prepare the stamping solution, 10 mM hexadecanethiol in absolute ethanol.
Prepare the backfilling solution, 1 mM glycol-terminated thiol in absolute ethanol.
Rinse the stamp with ethanol and dry thoroughly with N2 gas.
Apply stamping solution to the PDMS stamp dropwise until fully coated.
Dry the stamp thoroughly with N2 gas.
Gently press the stamp onto the gold substrate and allow the monolayer to form for 15 s.
Place the gold substrate into a petri dish containing 18.2 MΩ deionized water, ensuring the substrate is submerged.
Rinse the stamped substrate twice with ethanol, drying with N2 gas after each rinse.
Cover the substrate with backfilling solution and seal the dish with parafilm to prevent evaporation.
Allow the background monolayer to form in the dark for 12-14 h.
Remove the patterned coverslip from the backfilling solution.
Rinse twice with ethanol, drying with N2 gas after each rinse.
Place the patterned coverslip in a small petri dish or cell culture chamber.
Cover the coverslip with 500 μL to 1 mL of Dulbecco's Phosphate Buffered Saline (DPBS).
Add a concentrated solution of protein to the DPBS and mix by pipetting several times.
Incubate the protein mixture with the substrate at 37°C for 1 h.
Rinse the substrate thoroughly with DPBS (4-5x) to remove unbound protein.
Add approximately 500 μL of complete cell growth media after the first three rinses.
Replace the growth media used to rinse the substrate with fresh media.
Dissociate and count cells for plating onto the substrate.
Plate dissociated cells onto the substrate.
Fabricate a master in photoresist for PDMS stamps.
Expose AZ9245 coated silicon wafers to light with the desired pattern using direct-write lithography or mask aligner.
Create PDMS stamps by casting Sylgard 182 (or Sylgard 184) from the fabricated photoresist master.
Use photoresist masters multiple times to create many copies of the same stamp.
Harden the PDMS and remove stamps using a razor blade.
Visualize the resulting stamp under a microscope by placing it feature side down on a glass coverslip.
Mix concentrated protein solution thoroughly in DPBS before application.
Stamp the prepared protein solution evenly on the substrate.
Ensure proper handling during stamping to avoid partial transfer or collapse.
Maintain the patterned substrate submerged in buffer to prevent exposure to air.
Use water as a barrier for patterns with very small features and high aspect ratios.
